description.narrative:
Bankwatch is an association of non-profit environmental CSOs where the main focus is to act as watchdogs for investments financed by IFIs (EBRD, EIB, ADB). Bankwatch’s mission is to prevent investments made within the framework of international development cooperation from having negative consequences on the environment and social structures. In addition, Bankwatch works to promote the use of renewable energy and increase public engagement on these issues. Among other things, Bankwatch has developed a helpdesk where communities in the region can apply for support.
Through SIDA-financed support in the Western Balkans, the contribution will work towards two goals. 1. Prevent harmful measures in the energy sector from receiving financial and political support 2. Empower citizens to claim their rights

Bankwatch är en sammanslutning av icke vinstdrivande miljöinriktade CSOs där det främsta fokuset är att agera watchdogs till investeringar finansierade av IFIs (EBRD, EIB, ADB). Bankwatch har som uppdrag att motverka att investeringar gjorda inom ramen för internationellt utvecklingssamarbete får negativa konsekvenser för miljö och sociala strukturer. Dessutom verkar Bankwatch för att främja användandet av förnyelsebar energi och utöka engagemanget för dessa frågor bland allmänheten. Bankwatch har bland annat utvecklat en helpdesk där organisationer i regionen kan ansöka om stöd. Genom ett SIDA-finansierat stöd i Västra Balkan ska insatsen jobba mot två mål. 1.Förhindra att skadliga åtgärder inom energisektorn får ekonomiskt och politiskt stöd 2.Stärka medborgarna till att göra anspråk på sina rättigheter

The contribution has the overall goal to support green transformation in the region.
Goal 1: Prevent harmful measures in the energy sector from receiving financial and political support.
The energy sector (electricity and heat) has been identified as the biggest source of carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions not only worldwide but also in the Western Balkans. To accelerate the energy transformation and prevent the most serious impacts of the climate emergency, the energy sector needs to be decarbonised. Not only are the regions still heavily dependent on fossil fuels, but they lack alternatives and, crucially, political will to raise the level of ambition for seeking sustainable solutions. Therefore, Bankwatch will focus on halting the further use of fossil fuels in the energy sector through the following measures: preventing new coal power plants; closing or pushing existing facilities to comply with environmental standards; supporting decarbonisation of district heating systems; blocking coal-to-gas conversions; and lobbying for the implementation of just transition principles across the region.
Goal 2: Empower citizens to claim their rights.
Each year, the IFI's lend billions of euros to improve the living conditions of millions of people around the world. In countries where the rule of law is limited due to autocracy or corruption, IFIs often serve as the primary safeguard of democratic principles. IFIs are bound by the legislation and commitments of its shareholders, which are then translated into internal IFI policies. Although these policies are far from perfect, often not enforced, and hard for the IFIs to monitor, they remain valuable entry points for the public to participate in decisions that can potentially improve their lives. All too often, however, the projects that are intended to promote and develop healthy, sustainable living have the opposite effect, destroying livelihoods and lives, and causing irreversible damage to biodiversity and cultural heritage, loss of local livelihoods, further discrimination of already vulnerable groups and marginalisation of affected people in decision-making. These projects can include the construction of large hydro dams, transport corridors, regional infrastructure such as fossil gas pipelines and highways, the extraction of gold and critical raw materials, and solid waste management facilities.
To support citizens in their efforts to positively steer the direction of these investments, actively engage in political decision-making, and harness the potential of IFIs to uphold democratic principles to the fullest, Bankwatch commits to improving access to information and enhancing public participation, lobbying IFIs to improve their internal mechanisms and policies, and building the capacity of civil society and affected communities to reclaim their rights.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between Sida and the CEE Bankwatch Network
Beslut om insats: Bankwatch västra Balkan 2024 - 2027

description.narrative: This is the third Conclusion on Performance of this contribution which is only one and a half year old, since there were two changes of responsible officer. This is the first regular analytical CoP. I, responsible PO, joined the unit in august last year and took over as responsible PO in March 2025, three months ago. Since then we have had three meetings, at their office in Brussels in April, at the EBRD annual meeting in May and the annual meeting online in June. This is the second period of support to Bankwatch. The NGO has continued to deliver in a professional manner, like during the first phase. Bankwatch prioritizes to achieve change rather than to achieve attention, by prioritizing dialogue to wide publication. This is true especially in the case of Ukraine, where most information is kept unpublished, but also in other cases, where information produced by Bankwatch can be used countertothe purpose by actors with different geopolitical aims. In other cases, widespread public campaigns is opted for as the preferred method to achieve impact. Bankwatch is a partner of Sida also in the sense that it can also support our analysis and actions. Examples of additional results: Prior to becoming responsible for the contribution, I made use of Bankwatch intelligence to support our joint agenda, a just green transition in the Balkans. When taking over responsibility for the follow up of the Western Balkans Investment Framework (WBIF) and Sida's contribution to it, the material produced by Bankwatch was complementary to the official documentation received from the WBIF, and the same goes for Sida's follow up of EBRD. A new EU instrument was launched in 2024/2025 to speed up the accession process, the Regional Growth Facility. Sida formulated a proposal to exclude fossil fuels from the investment call ToRs with the support from Bankwatch. They provided information on the legal basis which stated that fossil fuels should not be eligible. Governments and other actors in the Balkans make references to Bankwatch analysis (reference series of Green Transition OECD conferences 2024/2025, f.ex. Sarajevo, January 2025). Expected results: Sammanfattande resultatuppdatering Conclusion on Performance Contribution ID: 16760 3 (8) The annual report is extensive and activity oriented, since the actual change also rely on larger political processes. Bankwatch seems to have an iterative approach, analyzing on where the processes can be influenced at a given moment to use resources wisely. The reporting covers each area of results/ activities. It shows that activities are advancing as expected. The following comment was sent to Bankwatch when approving the annual report: "Your report is restricted to project activities. Most reports also briefly cover aspects of context and its effects on the project, organizational developments, and comments on the budget execution to explain deviations, which helps connect the financial report to the narrative report. A more overarching analytical approach also makes it easier for us to understand suggestions for any change of direction with changes of plans or budgets if/when they are presented. A list of contents with references to page numbers also helps. Lets discuss further how the reporting can help us in the follow up of the project." In response, Bankwatch referred to its general annual report that responds to several of the above queries. We agreed that Bankwatch will look at possibilities to make the reporting more streamlined to avoid extra work only related to reporting on Sida's financial contribution. Examples of results reported (from the general annual report 2024 p.1214, 23/00154350): "Our advocacy led to the municipality abljak, Montenegro receiving technical assistance to rethink its district heating plans. The result? The municipality will now prioritise heat pumps instead of biomass and estimates a threeandahalffold reduction in investment costs." "Bankwatchs advocacy helped ensure that the Energy Communitys list of priority infrastructure projects was chosen under updated EU rules that exclude funding for fossil gas. We also successfully pushed for public consultations on this list and advised on how they should be conducted. The final list contains no projects that include fossil gas or hydrogen." "Following an NGO complaint and Energy Community mediation process, the Republika Srpska entity in Bosnia and Herzegovina committed to carry out a new environmental assessment for this proposed hydropower plant on the Drina, replacing the previous inadequate study and enabling new public consultations." "An investigation by the EBRD's independent project accountability mechanism (IPAM) found that the Corridor Vc highway project in Bosnia and Herzegovina violated the Bank's safeguards policy and the rights of affected people. It recommended new assessments of route alternatives and proper public consultations on environmental and social impacts." Sammanfattande resultatuppdatering Conclusion on Performance Contribution ID: 16760 4 (8) "The contract for the planned Tuzla 7 coal plant in Bosnia and Herzegovina was reported to be officially cancelled in April 2024, marking the end of a tenyear battle by Bankwatch and our partners. The new 450megawatt unit had been planned for almost two decades prior to this decision. The project had been plagued by legal challenges from NGOs Ekotim and the Aarhus Centre in Sarajevo, supported by Bankwatch, regarding its inadequate environmental impact assessment and a guarantee by the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina authorities for a loan from the China Eximbank. In 2021 the Energy Community Ministerial Council confirmed the loan guarantee was illegal." From the Sida report p.24, dox 23/00154343: "The EBRDs updated Environmental and Social Policy (ESP) and Access to Information Policy (AIP) include stronger safeguards for the rights of affected communities, including access to greater project information and participation in decisionmaking. The ESP included new requirements with regards to contextual and retaliation risk assessments as part of the due diligence process, including also stakeholders perspectives." "Gender work: The EBRDs revised ESP was significantly improved with regards to new definitions, banks commitments and requirements to clients with regards to gender based violence and harassment, gender identity and sexual orientation, sexual exploitation and abuse, as well as on equality and diversity of workforce. The EBRDs new Infrastructure Strategy has a strong focus on safety, affordability and accessibility of public infrastructure and services for vulnerable groups and underserved areas." "Sarajevo and Tbilisi were highlighted as cities that receive significant EBRD, EIB and ADB investment for public transport projects, with accent on the need for more reliable and safe services, especially in view of the diverse mobility needs of women and vulnerable groups. Bankwatch organised a gender webinar, later transformed into a podcast, where civil society from Georgia, BiH, North Macedonia and Serbia exchanged information and emerging good practice to prevent genderbased violence and harassment in public spaces and urban transport."
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
